query: High-entropy alloys contain five or more elements at 5–35 at% each, generally with comparable atomic radii. Refractory and nickel-based high-entropy alloys have demonstrated elevated-temperature mechanical properties comparable to titanium- and nickel-based alloys used in extreme environments because of their heat resistance and specific strength. However, prior investigations have mainly treated titanium and nickel as additions, leaving alloys in which both are primary constituents unexplored. Subject to the stated compositional definition, what single testable intervention hypothesis could improve the elevated-temperature mechanical properties of a titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy relative to the same material without the intervention? Specify the intervention, causal mechanism, predicted relative outcome, composition and operating boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a controlled addition of ≈5 at% molybdenum (Mo) into a titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy promotes the in situ formation of fine, Mo-rich precipitates at grain boundaries, which retards dislocation motion and grain boundary sliding and thereby enhances elevated-temperature mechanical properties.
generation.material_initial_state: A titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy without refractory-element modifications and with a relatively homogeneous microstructure.
generation.intervention: Adjust the alloy composition to include ≈5 at% Mo (with corresponding adjustments in other element percentages to maintain each within 5–35 at%), ensuring the high-entropy alloy criteria are met.
generation.conditions: Elevated-temperature mechanical testing (e.g., creep and yield strength measurements) at temperatures typically above 700°C up to 900°C, under constant load conditions that simulate extreme environment applications.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a fine, evenly distributed dispersion of Mo-rich precipitates (or nanophase segregations) at the grain boundaries.
generation.mechanism: Mo-rich precipitates act as barriers to dislocation movement and inhibit grain boundary sliding, thereby reducing creep rate and enhancing yield strength under high-temperature conditions.
generation.predicted_outcome: The Mo-modified alloy will exhibit lower creep rates and higher yield strength when evaluated at elevated temperatures compared to the baseline alloy without Mo.
generation.baseline: The original titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy lacking the Mo addition.
generation.boundary: The intervention should be applied under the constraint that all alloying elements remain within the 5–35 at% range and the mechanical benefits are evaluated within the temperature window of 700–900°C; composition adjustments must not compromise the high-entropy alloy phase stability.
generation.uncertainty: The stability and precise distribution of Mo-rich precipitates in a Ti-Ni primary high-entropy alloy system is currently unverified, and the degree of mechanical improvement may depend on subtleties in processing and phase evolution.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize two alloy batches: one being the titanium- and nickel-primary high-entropy alloy with ≈5 at% Mo addition (with adjusted composition) and one control alloy without Mo. Subject both to identical thermal-mechanical processing and perform high-temperature creep tests at 800°C under a constant applied load.
measurements: Creep rate measurements over a fixed duration
Yield strength determination via high-temperature tensile tests
Microstructural analysis (e.g., TEM, SEM) to detect and characterize any Mo-rich precipitates at grain boundaries
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Mo-added alloy does not statistically exhibit lower creep rates and higher yield strength than the control alloy at the tested temperature, or if microstructural characterization fails to reveal a significant population of Mo-rich precipitates, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.
